BLOCKER: `diff_reviews(committed=True)` raises `RuntimeError("review evidence tree is unreadable or empty")` when `HEAD` has no `engineering/reviews` entries. `evaluate()` turns that into a row error, `main()` returns 2, and the new precheck gate hard-fails every completion on any branch/repo with no committed reviews (first review, shallow CI checkout, history rewrite). Absence of reviews is a legitimate state, not an unreadable tree — empty must be a zero count, not exit 2.
MAJOR: `review_churn_check.main()` builds the base as `a.base or env or _git_text(["merge-base","develop","HEAD"]) or _git_text(["merge-base","origin/develop","HEAD"])`. If `_git_text` raises on non-zero exit (the pattern used elsewhere in this module), the `or` chain aborts at the first call and the documented `origin/develop` fallback is dead code — every repo without a local `develop` exits 2, contradicting docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md.

`architect_review.main()` calls `review_guard()` → `churn_verdict()` → `diff_reviews()` with no exception handling, so a missing/corrupt evidence dir surfaces as a raw traceback (exit 1) on the very first review, instead of the fail-closed message/exit-2 contract stated for the churn path.

`churn_attested()` accepts `latest_sha in note` as substring matching. Short shas (or a sha that is a substring of another) can satisfy an unrelated attestation, weakening the HIL escape hatch that is the only brake on unbounded re-review; require a token-boundary/full-sha match and reject empty `latest_sha`.

The `-prev-<ms>` archive naming plus the committed-tree reader means archived and current evidence for the same `sha` both count (asserted by `test_archived_rereview_counts_as_a_run`). A single re-review therefore contributes 2 to `count`, so a real 3-run sequence reads as 4 and trips the fail boundary one re-review early versus the documented "one diff review per freeze" budget semantics.
MINOR: `review_epoch()` takes the *last* Gate 1 entry in array order, not the max `at`; correctness depends on the ledger being strictly append-time-ordered. An out-of-order or replayed entry silently changes the epoch and the counted set.

`churn_verdict`/`evaluate` reach into privates (`ar._git_text`, `rc.g2.transitions`); a shared internal module or explicit public seams would avoid breakage from unrelated refactors in `architect_review.py`.

`redact_reason()` calls `review_budget()` (config load + validation) from inside a redaction helper; pass `reason_max_chars` in, or the redaction utility is untestable/unsafe to reuse without a valid config file.

`reason_flag_error` validation and `review_guard` validation are both surfaced in `main` with duplicated print/return-1 handling; consolidate to one guard entry point so a future mode cannot bypass the reason checks.
Row-level `except Exception` in `evaluate()` reports count=0/warn_after=0 in the error row, which leaks into `--json` output as plausible-but-false data; emit only `item` + `error` for error rows.
NIT: The `config/architect-review.json` diff reformats unrelated existing arrays (`blocking_findings`, `skip_globs`) into multi-line form, adding review noise to an otherwise additive change.
`redact_reason`'s cap is applied after redaction but at a fixed index, so a `[REDACTED...]` marker sitting at position 500 is clipped mid-token — cap to the last whitespace instead.

Test file omits blank lines between some consecutive `def`s (`test_bad_budget_config_fails_closed`/`test_reason_flag_requires_rereview`, `test_redact_url_and_pem`/`test_epoch_boundary_is_inclusive`), inconsistent with the repo's style checks.
Docs encode `warn_after`/`fail_after` values (2/4) in prose while the config is the source of truth; cite the key names only so config drift cannot falsify the doc.
SUMMARY: Solid single-owner design: thresholds, counting and verdict genuinely live in `architect_review.py` with no duplication, and the boundary/epoch/attestation/redaction tests are real. The committed-tree path, however, conflates "no reviews yet" with "unreadable tree", making the new precheck gate fail closed (exit 2) on any branch without committed evidence — that, plus the likely-dead `origin/develop` fallback and the double-count of archived `-prev-` files, means the budget will misfire in exactly the CI environments it is meant to protect. Fix the empty-tree semantics, harden sha citation, and land a graceful error path in `architect_review.main` before this gates completions.
